When buildManifest receives staleIds containing an ID in budgetExcludedIds, then that excludedChunks entry has reason equal to "budget", preserving the mechanical cause rather than replacing it.
When buildManifest receives staleIds containing an ID in belowMin, then that excludedChunks entry has stale equal to true.
When buildManifest receives staleIds containing an ID in dedupeDropped, then that excludedChunks entry has stale equal to true.
When buildManifest receives staleIds containing an ID in roleFiltered, then that excludedChunks entry has stale equal to true.

Given ContextOrchestrator.assemble receives two providers whose chunk content has trigram Jaccard similarity at or above SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD (src/context/engine/dedupe.ts:21, 0.9 — identical content satisfies it), and applyStaleness marks the lower-scoring chunk staleCandidate true with a scoreMultiplier below 1, when assembly dedupes the chunks, then the manifest excludedChunks entry for the dropped chunk has stale true and reason "dedupe".
When the rebuild path budget-excludes a packed chunk carrying staleCandidate true, then that rebuilt manifest excludedChunks entry has stale equal to true.
When the rebuild path budget-excludes a packed chunk carrying no staleCandidate, then that rebuilt manifest excludedChunks entry has stale equal to false.

userStories.title: Carry provider and staleness axes onto chunk observations

When collectObservations reads a manifest with no chunkProviders entry for an included chunk, then the emitted chunk-included observation payload omits provider.
When collectObservations reads a manifest whose chunkProviders maps an excluded chunk ID to "git-history", then the emitted chunk-excluded observation payload has provider equal to "git-history".
When collectObservations reads a manifest whose excludedChunks entry carries stale true, then the emitted chunk-excluded observation payload has stale equal to true.
When collectObservations reads a manifest whose excludedChunks entry carries stale false, then the emitted chunk-excluded observation payload has stale equal to false.

When runHeuristics receives chunk-excluded observations for one chunk ID carrying payload.stale equal to false across the same number of distinct runs, then it emits no H5 proposal.

routing.reasoning: This is a bounded two-module schema/projection change plus one existing heuristic predicate; its producer-consumer seam is straightforward to exercise in one test session.

modifiedFiles.reason: its H5 fixtures at lines 146 and 157 construct `chunk-excluded` payloads with `reason: "stale"` to make the heuristic fire. The replacing invariant: H5 fires on `payload.stale === true`, and `reason` on those fixtures carries the mechanical cause instead.

its fixture at line 327 writes `excludedChunks: [{ id: "rules:def", reason: "stale" }]` into a manifest file and line 410 asserts the emitted observation has `payload.reason === "stale"`. Both sit in the same test. The replacing invariant: the fixture expresses staleness as `stale: true` alongside the mechanical reason that excluded the chunk, and the assertion reads `payload.stale === true`. Note the fixture at line 327 is inside a `JSON.stringify` call and so is invisible to the typecheck gate — it will not fail the build, and must be changed deliberately.

userStories.title: Label proposals with real heuristic-window provenance
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Render both heuristic-window provenance and run-local counts, and retain the H6 feature prefix that its grouping key already has.

**Motivation** — A file headed "1294 observations" contained nothing derived from those 1,294 observations because the renderer labels the current run while heuristics consume the rollup window.

**Approach** — `renderProposals(proposals, runId, observationCount, provenance?)` receives provenance `{ runCount: number; observationCount: number }` describing the heuristic window. The header states the window the proposals derive from and the run's own count separately, so neither fact is lost. The fourth parameter is optional, and omitted `provenance` defaults to `{ runCount: 1, observationCount }` — the single-run reading, which is exactly correct for the dryrun. The post-run path has a window; when the window is empty and current observations are used instead, its provenance describes that fallback as one run. H6 proposal `storyIds` is `["<featureId>/<storyId>"]`, the same composite key its group was built under.

**Scope** — In: renderer interface/header and empty-proposal text, post-run window/fallback wiring, H6 identifier correction, and guide update. Out: automatic size-gated pruning belongs to US-004; collector axes belong to US-002; changing proposal file location, filename, or commit/show markdown structure remains excluded.

**Interface**
```typescript
renderProposals(
  proposals: Proposal[],
  runId: string,
  observationCount: number,
  provenance?: { runCount: number; observationCount: number },
): string
```

The two production callers are the post-run action, which has a window, and `curatorDryrun`, which uses one run's `observations.jsonl` and has no window. Existing three-argument callers remain valid, and the run's own observation count remains in the header.
acceptanceCriteria: When renderProposals receives provenance { runCount: 20, observationCount: 4000 } and a run observation count of 1294, then its header states both 20 runs and 4000 window observations.

When renderProposals receives provenance { runCount: 20, observationCount: 4000 } and a run observation count of 1294, then its header separately states the run's own count of 1294, distinctly from the window count.
When renderProposals receives provenance whose runCount is 1, then its header states one run, so the empty-window fallback is described as such rather than as a 20-run window.

When runHeuristics processes enough consecutive unchanged fix-cycle iteration observations for featureId "context-providers-22" and storyId "US-001" to meet unchangedOutcome, then its H6 proposal storyIds contains "context-providers-22/US-001".

When runHeuristics processes threshold-satisfying unchanged fix-cycle iteration observations for storyId "US-001" under two different featureId values, then it emits two distinct H6 proposals whose storyIds differ.

Given the curator post-run action has outputDir set and its rollup holds observations from more than one run, when it executes, then the written curator-proposals.md header states the window run count rather than 1.

When renderProposals is called with only three arguments, then its header states one run and a window observation count equal to the run's own observation count, preserving the correct single-run dryrun default.

Given the curator post-run action has outputDir set and an empty rollup, when it executes, then the written curator-proposals.md header states one run and a window observation count equal to the current run's own observation count rather than the zero runs returned by the empty window.
When renderProposals receives an empty proposal list, then its no-heuristics-fired line attributes its observation count to the heuristic window rather than to this run.

routing.reasoning: The work changes a backward-compatible public rendering signature, a cross-run post-run integration path, fallback semantics, heuristic identity, and documentation.

modifiedFiles.reason: 18 existing call sites pass `renderProposals` three arguments, and lines 28, 35, 103, 198 and 204 assert substrings of the current header. The replacing invariant: the three-argument form keeps working via the optional fourth parameter, the run's own observation count remains in the header, and this story's new criteria are added to this file. Lines 99-105 additionally assert on the zero-proposal line at `render.ts:40`, which still reads "No heuristics fired for this run" — the same per-run misattribution this story corrects — and must be reworded with it.

line 148 states "Each run produces a proposal file" and line 151 shows a sample header carrying only a run id, both of which teach the per-run reading this story corrects. The replacing invariant: the guide states that proposals derive from the rolling heuristic window and shows the corrected header.

userStories.title: Size-gate automatic rollup retention
acceptanceCriteria: When CuratorConfigSchema parses curator configuration with retention.pruneThresholdBytes unset, then the parsed retention.pruneThresholdBytes is 67108864.
When CuratorConfigSchema parses curator configuration with retention.keepRuns unset, then the parsed retention.keepRuns is 50.
When maybePruneRollup receives a rollup file whose size exceeds retention.pruneThresholdBytes, then it calls pruneRollup once with keepRunIds containing at most retention.keepRuns IDs.
When maybePruneRollup receives a rollup file whose size is below retention.pruneThresholdBytes, then it does not call pruneRollup.
When maybePruneRollup receives a rollup file whose size exactly equals retention.pruneThresholdBytes, then it does not call pruneRollup, because the gate opens above rather than at the threshold.
When pruneRollup rejects during maybePruneRollup, then maybePruneRollup resolves with pruned equal to false and an error string rather than propagating the rejection.
When maybePruneRollup receives a rollup path that does not exist, then it does not call pruneRollup and resolves without rejecting.
Given the curator post-run action has outputDir set and a rollup larger than configured retention.pruneThresholdBytes, when it executes, then it calls pruneRollup once.
Given the curator post-run action has outputDir set and a rollup smaller than configured retention.pruneThresholdBytes, when it executes, then it does not call pruneRollup.
Given the curator post-run action has outputDir set and pruneRollup rejects, when it executes, then its returned PostRunActionResult has success equal to true.

Given the curator post-run action has outputDir set and an over-threshold rollup evicts runs, when it executes, then observations.jsonl and curator-proposals.md remain present in each evicted run directory, preserving artifact deletion exclusively for manual gc.

When getCuratorRetention receives a post-run context carrying no curator configuration, then it returns pruneThresholdBytes 67108864 and keepRuns 50, matching the schema defaults despite the untyped post-run config.

routing.reasoning: This combines a new injectable filesystem gate, failure-isolated post-run integration, schema/type extraction constrained by a hard file-size limit, and preservation of manual-gc behavior.

outOfScope: **Out of scope (US-004 only):** concurrent invocation of the automatic prune and `nax curator gc` against the same rollup. Both already serialise through the path-keyed file lock that `pruneRollup` and `appendToRollup` share (`rollup-prune.ts:100`), and this story adds no new concurrency surface.

analysis:
This is an enhancement across the existing context-engine manifest pipeline and curator post-run plugin. `buildManifest` is a pure assembly function at `src/context/engine/manifest-builder.ts:49-154`; its four exclusion mappings currently emit only IDs and reasons at `:103-108`. The persisted `ContextManifest.excludedChunks` union still includes the dead `"stale"` reason at `src/context/engine/manifest-types.ts:150-153`. The sole production buildManifest call is in `src/context/engine/orchestrator.ts:369-455`: `scored` is available before dedupe/role/min-score/packing and is documented as the superset required to derive `staleIds`. Rebuild is a separate path that bypasses buildManifest and hand-builds budget exclusions in `src/context/engine/rebuild.ts:203-205`; it must inspect `packedChunks` for `staleCandidate`. Existing builder test input factories, notably `test/unit/context/engine/manifest-builder-eviction.test.ts:35-59`, must supply the new required input. Staleness classification itself remains untouched.

Curator collection reads persisted manifests defensively in `src/plugins/builtin/curator/collect.ts:275-342`. It currently forwards chunk summary/token data but drops `chunkProviders` and excluded stale attribution. The source contracts are `src/plugins/builtin/curator/types.ts:54-71`; optional additions preserve old manifests, and unknown provider mappings must result in omission rather than a synthetic value. H5 currently can never fire because `src/plugins/builtin/curator/heuristics.ts:320-325` filters on `reason === "stale"`; retargeting to the boolean flag retains its existing run-ID threshold/grouping. H6 already groups by feature/story composite key but emits the bare story ID at `src/plugins/builtin/curator/heuristics.ts:357-400`. The existing collector test is near its size cap, so the specified new chunk-axis test file is justified.

The post-run action at `src/plugins/builtin/curator/index.ts:83-143` appends observations, reads a project-scoped cross-run heuristic window, falls back to current observations when that window is empty, and calls the current three-argument renderer. `renderProposals` at `src/plugins/builtin/curator/render.ts:30-41` labels only the run-local count and misattributes its no-proposal wording. The dryrun caller in `src/commands/curator.ts:500-527` has only one run, so the renderer's provenance parameter must be optional. Existing post-run seam context construction and cross-run rollup use are demonstrated by `test/unit/plugins/builtin/curator-seam.test.ts:35-88`; post-run integration cases must set `outputDir`. The guide example at `docs/guides/curator.md:148-151` teaches the old per-run interpretation.

Retention must compose existing primitives, not replace them. `scanProjectRunIds` full-scans and returns newest-first project run IDs (`src/plugins/builtin/curator/rollup-prune.ts:55-68`); `pruneRollup` is locked, two-pass, and preserves other-project/unattributed rows (`:94-167`). `src/plugins/builtin/curator/rollup.ts:18-29` defines the 64 MiB maximum window tail and already uses Bun file APIs. Manual gc has a 50-run default and deletes run artifacts (`src/commands/curator.ts:533-579`), behavior automatic pruning must not replicate. Schema defaults belong in `src/config/schemas-infra.ts:440-468`. `src/config/runtime-types.ts` is exactly at the 600-line hard limit (`:550-600`), so all curator runtime interfaces must move to the new leaf file and be re-exported; hub exports in `src/config/types.ts:19-31` must continue to resolve. Risks are persisted-schema compatibility, losing the mechanical cause when adding stale attribution, falsely claiming window provenance during fallback, and allowing observer/prune filesystem failures to fail a successful run. No migration is needed: optional new fields leave historical manifests readable and prune preserves unknown/other-project rows.
outOfScope: Changing what `applyStaleness`, `detectContradictions` or `selectStaleByAge` classify as stale. This feature only attributes an existing signal; the detection rules are untouched.
Persisting `ChunkKind` onto the context manifest. It remains an in-memory field consumed by scoring and packing, and is neither persisted nor removed.

Deleting per-run curator artifacts (`observations.jsonl`, `curator-proposals.md`) from evicted run directories in the automatic prune path. That deletion stays exclusive to the manual `nax curator gc` subcommand; the automatic path prunes rollup rows only.
Changing the location, filename or markdown structure that `nax curator commit` and `nax curator show` parse out of `curator-proposals.md`. Only the header provenance line changes.
Fixing H1 recurrence detection (nax#1863). It is closed by ruling and must not be reopened here.
Adding any new heuristic. H5 is retargeted and H6 is corrected; no seventh heuristic is introduced.
